# Architecture Artifact Lifecycle Framework

**← Back to [EAP Home](../README.md) • [Foundation](./README.md)**

---

> This document defines the authoritative service architecture lifecycle for the Gainwell Enterprise Architecture Program — mapping every stage from service conceptualization through service delivery to the artifacts expected at that stage, the roles responsible for them, and their contributions to the Service Design Package (SDP) and Service Security Plan (SSP). It also defines where Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) specifications are introduced and how they connect to TOGAF architecture artifacts.

[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#11-purpose]

### 1.1 Purpose

This document provides:

1. A **stage-by-stage map** of all architecture artifacts expected across the service lifecycle
2. A **RACI matrix** defining who creates, reviews, approves, and maintains each artifact
3. **Content specifications** defining the minimum required sections and quality criteria for each artifact type
4. **BDD integration points** showing where and how Behavior-Driven Development specifications connect to TOGAF architecture artifacts
5. **Traceability tables** identifying which artifacts contribute to the Service Design Package (SDP) and Service Security Plan (SSP)
6. A **template index** linking to the authoritative template for each artifact type
page_texts.5:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#12-scope]

### 1.2 Scope

This framework applies to all Gainwell EA practice artifact production — regardless of business domain (application, infrastructure, business, information, technology, security) or delivery methodology (Agile, SAFe, waterfall). Domain-specific specializations (e.g., security TOGAF templates) extend this framework and follow the same stage-artifact mapping.

**Out of scope**: Governance artifacts (CRB submissions, ARB decisions), project management artifacts (project plans, sprint backlogs), and operational runbooks are not covered here.
page_texts.6:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#13-relationship-to-togaf-adm]

### 1.3 Relationship to TOGAF ADM

The nine stages in this framework map directly to TOGAF Architecture Development Method (ADM) phases:

| Lifecycle Stage | TOGAF ADM Phase |
|---|---|
| Stage 1 — Service Conceptualization | Phase A: Architecture Vision |
| Stage 2 — Capability & Business Architecture | Phase B: Business Architecture |
| Stage 3 — Architecture Design | Phases B–D: Business / Information / Technology Architecture |
| Stage 4 — Reference Architecture | Phase C–D: Information / Technology Architecture |
| Stage 5 — Behavioral Specification | Phase C–E: Information / Technology / Opportunities & Solutions |
| Stage 6 — Solution Design | Phase E: Opportunities & Solutions |
| Stage 7 — Delivery Planning | Phase F: Migration Planning |
| Stage 8 — Implementation Governance | Phase G: Implementation Governance |
| Stage 9 — Service Operations & Change | Phase H: Architecture Change Management |

> **Iterative ADM note**: TOGAF ADM is intentionally iterative — phases are revisited as understanding deepens or requirements evolve. This framework reflects the *primary* production window for each artifact, not a rigid waterfall sequence.

| Artifact | Required? | SDP? | SSP? | Template |

| Stakeholder Register | **Required** | ✓ | — | — |
| Service Concept / Problem Statement | **Required** | ✓ | — | — |
| Initial Risk Register | Recommended | — | ✓ | — |

[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#stage-2--capability--business-architecture-phase-b]

### Stage 2 — Capability & Business Architecture (Phase B)

**Purpose**: Define what the service must *do* in business terms. Map capabilities, processes, and value streams to architectural outcomes.

| Artifact | Required? | SDP? | SSP? | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Business Capability Map | **Required** | ✓ | — | — |
| Capability Descriptions | **Required** | ✓ | — | [Security variant](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/security-capability-descriptions-template.md) |
| Business Context Diagram | **Required** | ✓ | — | — |

**Stage gate**: Capabilities signed off by Business Analyst and Enterprise Architect before ABB authoring begins.

---
page_texts.11:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#stage-3--architecture-design-phases-bd]

### Stage 3 — Architecture Design (Phases B–D)

**Purpose**: Express the required capabilities as technology-agnostic Architecture Building Blocks (ABBs). ABBs define *what* the architecture must deliver, not *how* it is implemented.

| Artifact | Required? | SDP? | SSP? | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Composite ABB | **Required** | ✓ | ✓ (if security-relevant) | [General ABB](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/abb-definition-template.md) · [Security ABB](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/security-abb-definition-template.md) |
| Component ABB (one per L2 capability) | **Required** | ✓ | ✓ (if security-relevant) | [General ABB](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/abb-definition-template.md) · [Security ABB](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/security-abb-definition-template.md) |
| ABB Catalog / Traceability Matrix | **Required** | ✓ | — | [Security ABB Catalog](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/security-abb-catalog-template.md) |
| Domain / Conceptual Model | Recommended | ✓ | — | — |

**Stage gate**: All Component ABBs reviewed by Enterprise Architect and relevant domain architects before RAD authoring begins. ABBs must not reference specific products or vendors.

---
page_texts.12:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#stage-4--reference-architecture-phase-cd]

### Stage 4 — Reference Architecture (Phase C–D)

**Purpose**: Provide illustrative architecture patterns and logical component guidance for realizing each Component ABB. RADs describe one valid approach — they are informative, not prescriptive for product selection.

| Artifact | Required? | SDP? | SSP? | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reference Architecture Document / RAD (one per Component ABB) | **Required** | ✓ | ✓ (if security-relevant) | [General RAD](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/abb-rad-template.md) · [Security RAD](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/security-reference-architecture-template.md) |
| Data Architecture / Data Model | Required for data-intensive services | ✓ | ✓ (if contains PII/PHI) | — |
| API Contract / Interface Specification | Required for integration services | ✓ | — | — |
| Architecture Compliance Criteria | **Required** | ✓ | ✓ | — |

**Stage gate**: RADs peer-reviewed by at least one additional Enterprise Architect or domain SME. RADs must not mandate specific products.

---
page_texts.13:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#stage-5--behavioral-specification-phase-ce]

### Stage 5 — Behavioral Specification (Phase C–E)

**Purpose**: Express the expected behaviors of architecture capabilities as testable Given/When/Then scenarios. BDD Specifications bridge the abstract intent of ABBs/RADs with the executable acceptance tests that delivery teams will use. See [§6.0 BDD Integration](#60-bdd-integration) for full detail.

| Artifact | Required? | SDP? | SSP? | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BDD Specification (one per Component ABB minimum) | **Required** | ✓ | ✓ (for security-relevant ABBs) | [BDD Specification](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/bdd-specification-template.md) |
| Feature Files / Gherkin Scenarios | **Required** | — | — | Derived from BDD Specification |
| Behavioral Contract (formal) | Optional | ✓ | ✓ | — |

**Stage gate**: BDD Specification reviewed by Business Analyst (scenario accuracy), Solution Architect (technical completeness), and QA Lead (testability) before Stage 6 begins.

---
page_texts.14:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#stage-6--solution-design-phase-e]

### Stage 6 — Solution Design (Phase E)

**Purpose**: Select specific products, platforms, and configurations (Solution Building Blocks) that realize the Component ABBs. SBBs are technology-specific and vendor-named. BDD Specifications from Stage 5 are refined to target the selected SBBs.

| Artifact | Required? | SDP? | SSP? | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Solution Building Block / SBB (one per product/platform realization) | **Required** | ✓ | ✓ (if security-relevant) | [General SBB](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/sbb-template.md) · [Security SBB](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/security-sbb-template.md) |
| Technology Selection Matrix | **Required** | ✓ | — | — |
| Integration Architecture | Required for multi-system services | ✓ | — | — |
| Security Architecture (if not covered by security SBBs) | **Required** | — | ✓ | — |

**Stage gate**: SBBs and Technology Selection Matrix reviewed by Enterprise Architect and Security Architect before Delivery Planning begins.

---
page_texts.15:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#stage-7--delivery-planning-phase-f]

### Stage 7 — Delivery Planning (Phase F)

**Purpose**: Aggregate all prior artifacts into the two primary governance outputs: the Service Design Package (SDP) and Service Security Plan (SSP). Produce the implementation plan.

| Artifact | Required? | SDP? | SSP? | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Service Design Package (SDP) | **Required** | — | — | Initial assembly from Stage 1–6 artifacts; Stage 8–9 outputs appended post-delivery |
| Service Security Plan (SSP) | **Required** | — | — | Assembled from security-relevant artifacts |
| Implementation Plan | **Required** | ✓ | — | — |
| Updated Risk Register | **Required** | — | ✓ | — |

**Stage gate**: SDP and SSP reviewed and approved by Enterprise Architect (SDP) and Security Architect (SSP) before implementation begins.

---
page_texts.16:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#stage-8--implementation-governance-phase-g]

### Stage 8 — Implementation Governance (Phase G)

**Purpose**: Oversee implementation, validate that what is built conforms to the approved architecture, and capture deviations.

| Artifact | Required? | SDP? | SSP? | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture Compliance Review (ACR) | **Required** | ✓ (appended) | ✓ (appended) | — |
| Architecture Change Request | As needed | ✓ (appended) | — | [ADR](../resources/work-templates/assets/artifacts/architecture-decision-record.md) |
| Implementation Verification Checklist | **Required** | ✓ (appended) | — | — |

**Stage gate**: Architecture Compliance Review signed off by Enterprise Architect and ARB (if material changes) before service launch.

---
page_texts.17:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#stage-9--service-operations--change-phase-h]

### Stage 9 — Service Operations & Change (Phase H)

**Purpose**: Manage ongoing architectural changes, evaluate the effectiveness of the architecture, and initiate re-entry to Stage 1 for material evolution.

| Artifact | Required? | SDP? | SSP? | Template |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Post-Implementation Review | **Required** | ✓ (appended) | — | — |
| Architecture Change Management Record | As needed | ✓ (appended) | ✓ (if security-relevant) | — |
| Lessons Learned | Recommended | — | — | — |

## 5.0 Artifact Content Specifications

The following table defines the **minimum required content** for each artifact type. These are quality floors — not ceilings.

| Artifact Type | Required Sections | Quality Criteria | When to Use vs. Related Types |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Architecture Vision** | Executive summary; stakeholder concerns; problem statement; architectural scope; success criteria; constraints and assumptions; normative language convention | Must be approved before any ABB work begins; must name stakeholders and scope boundaries explicitly | Use before any detailed architecture; do not use as a substitute for capability descriptions or ABBs |
| **Capability Descriptions** | Capability name; L1/L2 hierarchy position; description; business outcomes; key processes; success indicators; related capabilities | One description per L2 capability; tied to a parent Vision | Use to describe *what* a capability delivers in business terms; do not include implementation details |
| **Composite ABB** | Metadata (GUID, ADM phase, type); architecture vision reference; normative language convention; ABB scope (in/out); related component ABBs; behavioral contract summary | Must be technology-agnostic; must not reference specific products; must list all child Component ABBs | Use as the parent container for a capability domain; do not create a Composite ABB without a Vision |
| **Component ABB** | Metadata (GUID, ADM phase, parent composite); architecture vision reference; capability statement; scope (in/out); behavioral requirements (SHALL/SHOULD/MAY); interface contracts; security controls; related Component ABBs | Technology-agnostic; every SHALL requirement must be testable via BDD Specification; no vendor names | Use for individual L2 capabilities; do not duplicate requirements across sibling Component ABBs |
| **ABB Catalog** | Traceability table (GUID, name, type, domain, ADM phase, status, RAD link, SBB link); coverage gaps analysis | Must be kept current as ABBs are added or updated; generated from ABB metadata | Use as the single traceability index for all ABBs in a capability domain |
| **Reference Architecture Document (RAD)** | Metadata (GUID, paired ABB, ADM phase); informative content notice; purpose and scope; platform engineering scope; control responsibility matrix; logical architecture; architecture diagram; implementation guidance; governance guidance | Informative only — does not mandate products; diagrams use logical names (no vendor logos); paired 1:1 with a Component ABB | Use to illustrate *how* a capability could be delivered; do not use as a design specification for a specific product |
| **BDD Specification** | Metadata (GUID, source ABB, source RAD, ADM phase); feature description; behavioral scope (in/out); traceability to ABB SHALL requirements; Given/When/Then scenarios (minimum 2 per ABB SHALL); edge cases and negative scenarios; glossary of domain terms used in scenarios | Every ABB SHALL must map to at least one scenario; scenarios must be testable without knowing the implementing technology; no implementation-specific details in Phase C–E BDD Specs | Use to express expected behaviors traceable to ABBs; do not use as a substitute for ABBs; refine in Phase E to target specific SBBs |
| **Solution Building Block (SBB)** | Metadata (GUID, realized ABB, paired RAD, ADM phase, product name/version); TOGAF ADM note; architecture vision reference; document hierarchy; solution overview; ABB capability realized; capability delivery matrix (how product features map to ABB SHALLs); implementation requirements; configuration guidance; integration patterns; governance and compliance; known limitations | Must reference a parent Component ABB and RAD; must address every ABB SHALL; must document known gaps between product capability and ABB requirements | Use for specific product/version implementations; do not use as architecture guidance (that's the ABB/RAD) |
| **Service Design Package (SDP)** | Cover sheet (service name, version, approval signatures); table of contents; Architecture Vision reference; Capability Map; ABB inventory; RAD references; BDD Specifications index; SBB inventory; Technology Selection rationale; Implementation Plan; ACR results; Risk Register | Assembled from existing artifacts — does not introduce new content; must be approved before implementation begins | Use as the single governance hand-off document to delivery; update with ACR and PIR as appendices post-delivery |
| **Service Security Plan (SSP)** | Cover sheet; security scope from Architecture Vision; security ABBs (with SHALL requirements); security RAD references; security BDD Specifications; security SBBs; Risk Register (security risks); security compliance checklist | Must be reviewed by Security Architect; must map every security ABB SHALL to an SBB realization or a documented gap with accepted risk | Use as the security governance companion to the SDP; never merge into the SDP — maintain as a separate document |

[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#61-where-bdd-enters-the-lifecycle]

### 6.1 Where BDD Enters the Lifecycle

BDD Specifications are introduced at **Stage 5 (Phase C–E)**, after RADs have been produced and before SBBs are selected.

The production window spans two TOGAF phases deliberately:

- **Phase C–D** (alongside RADs): Initial BDD Specifications are authored. They express the behavioral contracts that any valid implementation of the ABB must honor. At this point, they are technology-agnostic — they describe what the system *must do*, not what product achieves it.

- **Phase E** (alongside SBB selection): BDD Specifications are refined and expanded to reflect the specific SBB selected. Scenarios that were technology-agnostic are augmented with SBB-specific context (e.g., specific API endpoint paths, product-specific configuration states). The original technology-agnostic scenarios are preserved — the SBB-specific extension is additive.
page_texts.25:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#62-how-architecture-artifacts-inform-bdd-specifications]

### 6.2 How Architecture Artifacts Inform BDD Specifications

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    VISION["Architecture Vision\n(Phase A)\nDefines: scope, success criteria"]
    ABB["Component ABB\n(Phase B–D)\nDefines: SHALL/SHOULD/MAY\nbehavioral requirements"]
    RAD["Reference Architecture (RAD)\n(Phase C–D)\nDefines: logical components,\ninterfaces, data flows"]
    BDD["BDD Specification\n(Phase C–E)\nExpresses: Given/When/Then\nscenarios per ABB SHALL"]
    SBB["Solution Building Block (SBB)\n(Phase E–F)\nBinds: product to ABB\nvia BDD Specification"]
    FEATURE["Feature Files\n(Gherkin / .feature)\nDeliverable: executable\nacceptance tests for dev teams"]

    VISION -->|"authorizes"| ABB
    ABB -->|"informs behavioral contracts"| RAD
    ABB -->|"SHALL requirements\nbecome scenario conditions"| BDD
    RAD -->|"logical interfaces\nbecome Given/When contexts"| BDD
    BDD -->|"scenarios refined\nfor specific product"| SBB
    BDD -->|"transformed into"| FEATURE

    style BDD fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#4caf50
    style FEATURE fill:#e8f5e9,stroke:#4caf50
```

**Key mapping rules:**

| ABB Element | BDD Specification Translation |
|---|---|
| Every `SHALL` requirement | Minimum one `Scenario` (happy path) + one negative/edge case `Scenario` |
| Every `SHOULD` requirement | Minimum one `Scenario` tagged `@recommended` |
| Scope "In Scope" items | Each becomes a Feature description or Feature section |
| Scope "Out of Scope" items | Each becomes a `Scenario Outline` tagged `@out-of-scope` that documents the excluded behavior |
| Interface contracts | Each interface becomes a `Background` or `Given` step in related scenarios |
| Security controls | Security-relevant SHALLs generate scenarios tagged `@security` and are reflected in the SSP |
page_texts.26:
[foundation/artifact-lifecycle-framework.md#63-bdd-specification-artifact-definition]

### 6.3 BDD Specification Artifact Definition

**Definition**: A BDD Specification is an architecture-layer artifact that expresses the expected behaviors of an architecture capability (as defined in a Component ABB) as structured, human-readable, and technology-agnostic Gherkin Given/When/Then scenarios. It serves as the behavioral contract between the architecture team (who defines what must be done) and the delivery team (who implements and tests it).

**Relationship to adjacent artifact types:**

| Artifact | Relationship to BDD Specification |
|---|---|
| Component ABB | BDD Specification is derived from the ABB's SHALL/SHOULD requirements; every ABB SHALL maps to at least one scenario |
| RAD | RAD logical interfaces and data flows inform the Given/When context in BDD scenarios |
| SBB | SBB is evaluated against BDD scenarios; SBB-specific extensions to scenarios are written in Phase E |
| Feature File (.feature) | Feature files are the delivery-ready Gherkin transformation of BDD Specification scenarios; QA and developers own feature files; architects own BDD Specifications |
| User Story | User Stories may contain acceptance criteria in Given/When/Then format; BDD Specifications are the architecture-layer refinement of those criteria into a complete behavioral contract |

**GUID placement in the document chain:**

```
GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-VISION-0.D.NN       (Phase A — Architecture Vision)
GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-ABB-1.D.NN          (Phase B–D — Composite ABB)
GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-2.D.NN       (Phase B–D — Component ABB)
GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-RAD-3.D.NN   (Phase C–D — Reference Architecture)
GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-BDD-3.5.D.NN (Phase C–E — BDD Specification) ← NEW
GUID-<DOMAIN>-<CAP>-<TYPE>-SBB-4.D.NN   (Phase E–F — Solution Building Block)
```

The `3.5` position reflects BDD's role: **after** the RAD establishes the logical architecture (3.x), **before** the SBB commits to a specific implementation (4.x). This placement encodes the dependency: BDD Specifications depend on ABBs and RADs, and SBBs are evaluated against BDD Specifications.

## 7.0 Service Design Package (SDP) Traceability

The SDP is the primary governance hand-off artifact from the architecture team to the delivery team. It is assembled from existing artifacts — it does not introduce new architectural content.

| Artifact | SDP Section | Stage Produced | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture Vision | Executive Summary + Scope | Stage 1 | Include approval signature |
| Stakeholder Register | Stakeholder Summary | Stage 1 | Summarize; full register as appendix |
| Business Capability Map | Capability Overview | Stage 2 | Include visual diagram |
| Composite ABB | Architecture Building Blocks — Overview | Stage 3 | Reference by GUID; include scope table |
| Component ABBs (all) | Architecture Building Blocks — Detail | Stage 3 | Reference by GUID; include SHALL summary |
| ABB Catalog | Architecture Building Blocks — Catalog | Stage 3 | Full traceability table |
| RADs (all) | Reference Architectures | Stage 4 | Reference by GUID; include architecture diagrams |
| BDD Specifications (all) | Behavioral Contracts | Stage 5 | Reference by GUID; include scenario summary |

## 8.0 Service Security Plan (SSP) Traceability

The SSP is the security-specific governance companion to the SDP. It is assembled from the security-relevant subset of lifecycle artifacts.

| Artifact | SSP Section | Stage Produced | Security-Specific Content Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| Architecture Vision | Security Scope | Stage 1 | Security stakeholders, security success criteria, security constraints |
| Initial Risk Register | Initial Security Risks | Stage 1 | Security-relevant risks with initial severity rating |
| Security ABBs (composite/component) | Security Architecture — Building Blocks | Stage 3 | Full SHALL/SHOULD requirements; security control categories |
| Security RADs | Security Architecture — Reference | Stage 4 | Security control responsibility matrix; security data flows |
| Security BDD Specifications | Security Behavioral Contracts | Stage 5 | All `@security`-tagged scenarios; link to ABB SHALL requirements |
| Security SBBs | Security Solution — Building Blocks | Stage 6 | Product-specific security configuration requirements; known gaps vs. ABB SHALLs |
| Updated Risk Register | Security Risk Summary | Stage 7 | Accepted risks with owner and remediation timeline; open risks |
| Architecture Compliance Review (security items) | Security Compliance Verification | Stage 8 | Security-specific compliance findings; deviations with accepted risk |

## 10.0 Glossary Additions

The following terms defined in this document should be added to [`foundation/glossary.md`](./glossary.md):

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **BDD Specification** | An architecture-layer artifact that expresses the expected behaviors of an architecture capability (as defined in a Component ABB) as structured, technology-agnostic Gherkin Given/When/Then scenarios. It serves as the behavioral contract between the architecture team and the delivery team, and is derived from ABB SHALL/SHOULD requirements. Position in TOGAF ADM: Phase C–E. GUID type: `-BDD-3.5.x`. |
| **Service Design Package (SDP)** | The primary governance hand-off document from the architecture team to the delivery team. Assembled from Stage 1–8 artifacts; does not introduce new architectural content. Approved by the Enterprise Architect before implementation begins. |
| **Service Security Plan (SSP)** | The security-specific governance companion to the SDP. Assembled from security-relevant lifecycle artifacts. Reviewed and approved by the Security Architect. Maintained as a separate document from the SDP. |
| **Architecture Lifecycle Stage** | One of nine defined stages in the Gainwell EA service architecture lifecycle, each mapping to a TOGAF ADM phase and producing one or more required artifacts. |
| **Behavioral Contract** | The set of testable behavioral expectations for an architecture capability, expressed as Given/When/Then scenarios in a BDD Specification. Every Component ABB SHALL requirement must be represented in a behavioral contract. |
| **Feature File** | A `.feature` file written in Gherkin syntax. Feature files are the delivery-ready transformation of BDD Specification scenarios. QA and development teams own feature files; architects own BDD Specifications. |
